steps: Ribosomes are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
items.finalAnswer: Ribosomes are made of rRNA and proteins.

steps: Chromosomes are made up of DNA and proteins.
items.finalAnswer: Chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins.

steps: The fluid mosaic model describes the structure of the cell membrane.
The membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer, with protein molecules embedded in it.
The phospholipid molecules and some proteins can move within the membrane, making it fluid.
The proteins are scattered in the phospholipid bilayer like a mosaic.
The membrane is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
items.finalAnswer: The cell membrane is a fluid phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins arranged like a mosaic.

steps: The cell wall is a non-living, rigid outer covering found outside the cell membrane of plant cells.
It is mainly made of cellulose and is freely permeable.
It gives the cell shape, strength and support.
It protects the cell and prevents it from bursting when water enters.
items.finalAnswer: The cellulose cell wall is a rigid, freely permeable covering that supports, protects and gives shape to the plant cell.

steps: The nucleus is surrounded by a double membrane called the nuclear envelope.
The nuclear envelope has pores that allow the exchange of materials between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
The nucleus contains a jelly-like substance called nucleoplasm.
A nucleolus is present in the nucleoplasm and helps in the formation of ribosomes.
The nucleus also contains chromatin, made of DNA and proteins; it forms chromosomes during cell division.
The nucleus controls the activities of the cell and contains hereditary material.
items.finalAnswer: The nucleus contains a nuclear envelope, nucleoplasm, nucleolus and chromatin, and controls cell activities.

steps: Lysosomes are small, membrane-bound sacs containing digestive enzymes.
They digest food particles, worn-out cell parts and foreign materials; they may also bring about self-digestion of a damaged cell.
The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a network of membrane-bound channels and flattened sacs in the cytoplasm.
Rough ER has ribosomes on its surface and helps in the synthesis and transport of proteins.
Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and helps in the synthesis of lipids.
items.finalAnswer: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes, while rough and smooth ER help in protein and lipid synthesis, respectively, and in transport.

steps: The Golgi complex consists of stacks of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
Vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum carry materials to the Golgi complex.
The Golgi complex modifies, sorts and packages these materials into vesicles.
These vesicles transport materials within the cell or secrete them outside the cell.
The Golgi complex also helps in the formation of lysosomes.
items.finalAnswer: The Golgi complex receives materials from the ER, modifies and packages them into vesicles for transport or secretion, and helps form lysosomes.
